title: Active Directory Lateral Movement
summary: Mapped lateral movement paths through an AD environment using Pass-the-Hash and Kerberoasting techniques, building detection coverage for common attack patterns.
scenario: Once an attacker compromises a single machine in an AD environment, they pivot laterally to reach high-value targets like domain controllers. Understanding these paths is essential for building detection rules.
objective: Identify and document lateral movement techniques in a lab AD environment to build detection coverage and monitoring checklists.
keyFindings: Kerberoasting tickets have detectable TGS request patterns in DC logs
Pass-the-Hash leaves NTLM authentication anomalies that can be correlated
BloodHound graph analysis reveals shortest attack paths for privilege escalation
Detection rules should focus on abnormal TGS request volumes and NTLM logon patterns
outcome: Built AD security monitoring checklist and detection rules for lateral movement indicators, covering Kerberoasting, Pass-the-Hash, and privilege escalation patterns.
